title: Ember and Spire
premise: Ines Galloway has spent years making himself unremarkable: a royal food-taster whose poison immunity is his only value, and a smuggler who knows every hidden pass through the Thornfell mountains. When a scholar's century-old prophecy book names him by a name he abandoned long ago, Ines learns he sold a piece of his soul as a child to the court beneath the mountain to survive, and that the usurper's armies intend to claim it and the power it holds. Hunted by prophecy-zealots and the usurper's inquisitors alike, he gathers an unlikely found family—a disgraced scholar, a deserting soldier, and a thief who claims to have known him before—to steal his soul back from the Spire. At the climax, Ines must choose between reclaiming his whole self and shattering the soul so no tyrant can ever wield it; he chooses to break it, discovering that identity was never something stored away but something built with the people beside him.
about_author: Bram Thornbury is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working mountain lodges across three countries, feeding strangers and collecting their stories. Ember and Spire is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Salt Road North.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ines Galloway tastes the king's supper, detects hemlock in the wine, and quietly saves a court that would never mourn him. That night, a scholar named Odile Vane shows him a prophecy book naming 'the Galloway boy' and tomorrow's date. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the uneasy pride of a man whose invisibility is both armor and cage.

chapters.title: What the Book Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile deciphers more of the prophecy: it describes Ines's childhood flight through Thornfell and promises his soul 'sleeps below the Spire.' Ines dismisses it until the passage names the lullaby only his dead mother sang. POV: Ines, with Odile's interjections. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past he buried reaching up to claim him.

chapters.title: Roads Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Inquisitors arrive hunting the prophecy's subject; Ines flees the capital using a smuggler's pass only he knows. On the road he rescues Dara, a deserter from the usurper's army, who recognizes him from wanted sketches. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reluctant trust kindling between two people who've survived by being alone.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Knew Him
chapters.summary: In a free-city safehouse, the thief Wren greets Ines by his forgotten childhood name and claims they were neighbors before the mountain took them both. Ines refuses to believe her—until she hums the lullaby. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief for a self that others remember better than you do.

chapters.title: Zealots at the Gate
chapters.summary: Prophecy-worshippers besiege the safehouse, believing Ines's soul will crown their messiah. The four escape into the deep tunnels, where Odile reveals the usurper's armies march on the free cities within weeks. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: guilt—Odile brought the prophecy to light and set the hunt in motion.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Following Wren's half-remembered maps, the group descends toward the Spire and finds the court below: a gilded underworld where sold souls are kept as currency. They see Ines's soul—a small ember of light—and learn it powers the usurper's war-machines. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at what his survival cost.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: To reach the vault, Ines must trade a memory of equal weight; he offers his mother's face. Dara objects, insisting there's another way, and the group fractures over whether some losses are too high. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument—Dara refusing to let Ines erase himself to save everyone.

chapters.title: Ember
chapters.summary: Ines trades the memory, reclaims his soul, and the Spire begins to collapse as its engines fail. The usurper's forces breach the tunnels; Wren is gravely wounded holding the escape route. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss—he is whole again, and it may not be enough.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: Cornered above ground with armies closing on the free cities, Ines realizes a whole soul can still be stolen again. He chooses to shatter it into every person who stood by him, making it unstealable forever. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity—identity given away freely cannot be taken.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Five
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the free cities hold, the usurper's machines are dark, and Ines runs a small kitchen at Thornfell's edge. His memories are incomplete, but Wren, Dara, and Odile fill the gaps nightly, telling him who he was. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—family as the memory that outlasts the self.
